requested_scope: Add tests, provide English versions of all Japanese material, and expand support toward all 7,126 distinct Intel Intrinsics Guide 3.6.9 names.
completed: The original shared-ABI suite was expanded from 254 to 268 registered intrinsic names, including 14 zero/aligned-memory/partial-memory operations.
The 268-case native adversarial suite passed 219 tests on each of Intel, ARM, OpenPOWER and RISC-V: 876 test executions, 288740 ABI calls, 3464504 lane checks. Additional RISC-V VLEN256 tests passed.
New tests exposed OpenPOWER signaling-NaN changes in set/setr/set_scalar/shuffle. The implementations were corrected without weakening expectations.

The adversarial input profile generates up to 512 distinct inputs per operation and respects finite input domains. All comparisons retain complete difference JSONL; HTML and standalone replay bundles have explicit limits.
English READMEs, JSON guides, reports and Studio language switching were added. The bilingual presentation regression suite passed 96 tests.

The separate SIMDe pure-value backend completed processing of all 1895 candidates in four environments using 60392 distinct inputs. All candidates compiled. ARM, OpenPOWER and RISC-V each executed all 1895 candidates with 60392 ok input records. Intel executed 552 candidates with 17540 ok records; CPU-feature guards recorded 1343 candidates and 42852 inputs as unsupported_cpu. This is execution evidence, not complete specification conformance.
A separate masked backend generates 233 candidate implementations. Initial Intel/ARM compilation and focused tests passed; the final catalog representation change still needs revalidation.
SoftFloat-backed packed FP16 arithmetic implements 117 signatures. All portable lane/mask test cases and the Intel reference compilation check passed; four-architecture comparison remains incomplete.
An AMX explicit-state implementation covers 27 entry points and passed focused local tests. Four-architecture checks and CLI integration remain incomplete.
known_findings: Independent portable-model tests retain the previous 2159 findings and detected an additional 9010 rounding-extension findings in a separate run. No clean aggregate quality run is claimed.
Unavailable Intel CPU instructions are recorded as unsupported/not comparable, not replaced with SIMDe or SoftFloat reference values.

Among 17540 inputs executable on both Intel and each target, raw return-byte differences were ARM 1008, OpenPOWER 981 and RISC-V 1735. Approximate reciprocal/rsqrt results and undefined upper cast bits require per-API interpretation; no raw verdict was rewritten. FP exception flags are diagnostic-only observations.
